newsitem.title: UK: Fitch rates Coca-Cola 2036 notes at A plus.
newsitem.headline: Fitch rates Coca-Cola 2036 notes at A plus.

text.p: Fitch Investors Service said on Wednesday it had rated Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc's $300 million senior notes due 2036 at A plus.
"The proceeds will be used to reduce the company's commercial paper borrowings," Fitch said.

"Coke Enterprises' rating was last affirmed in June 1996 following the company's announcement that it intends to acquire the Coca-Cola bottling operations in Great Britain, Belgium and most of France for a combined purchase price of $2.7 billion, net of acquired debt," it said in a statement.
Fitch said the rating reflects the company's position as the world's largest beverage bottler, its geographic diversity and the imputed credit support from The Coca-Cola Company.
"Also considered is the near-term stress the recent international acquisitions will place on the company's bondholder protection measures," it said.
"Pro forma for the acquisitions, the company's international operations are expected to account for approximately 28 percent of its volume."
"The additional volume further emphasizes Coke Enterprises' strategic position in the Coca-Cola system and strengthens the implicit credit support of The Coca-Cola Company," Fitch said.
The rating agency said it viewed the decline in bondholder protection measures as temporary and expected management to improve them through a combination of EBITDA growth and debt reduction.

"Cash available for debt reduction is expected to come from the company's existing $150 million of net free cash flow and the European acquisitions, which are expected to be cash flow positive in their first year of operation," it said.
"However, to the extent that the company's future acquisition strategy permanently increases leverage above historical levels, long-term credit quality could be impaired," Fitch added.
